answer.original_source: NN, Inc. (announcement, undated in record; relayed by finance.yahoo.com on 2026-07-01)
answer.new_information: The record supports that NN, Inc. announced in late June 2026 an expansion of 47 machine centers at its Wuxi, China plant for liquid cooling production, and that NN said 100% of the new capacity was pre-sold under multi-year, multi-product awards and targeted US$80–US$90 million of new 2026 business. Material unknowns: the customer(s) are not named by NN in the record; the NVIDIA link comes from article framing ('for NVIDIA AI data center racks'); the exact announcement day, award values, award periods, capex amount and ramp timing are absent; the revenue and earnings projections are a third-party narrative and an unnamed analyst estimate, not NN guidance. Evidence needed: an NN filing or press release naming the customer and award terms, and shipment or qualification confirmation from NVIDIA or its rack builders before this can be tied to NVDA sales.
answer.independent_judgement: Not proposed as a new question: the record concerns NN, Inc., which is outside the covered scope (NVDA only), and its NVIDIA connection is an article's framing rather than a stated customer relationship. A supplier's pre-sold capacity plan could inform supply-chain monitoring for NVDA rack ramps, but it does not establish NVDA revenue. The narrative fair-value and revenue figures are third-party and rumour-tier, so they carry no weight for the NVDA record.
answer.reason: The source is a supplier-side announcement about a non-covered company, with no stored NVDA questions or pieces to update. Its NVIDIA link is not established by NN, and the projections are third-party or rumour, so the record is kept as background context only.
